outcome: Ultrastructural changes in placental tissue (abnormal organelles, virus-like particles)
Immunological profile (infiltration of CD68+ and TCD8+ cells, expression of MMPs, cytokines like IFN-g and TNF-a, RANTES/CCL5, VEGFR-2)
Neuronal damage in the developing fetus (modulated by BDNF decrease)
cohort: The study involved placental tissues obtained from ten pregnant women infected with ZIKV (five resulting in fetal microcephaly and five without) and five non-infected control pregnant women during the 2015-2016 Brazilian epidemic.
finding: ZIKV infection during pregnancy caused severe histopathological and ultrastructural damage to the placenta, accompanied by excessive inflammation, vascular permeability dysfunction, and a decrease in BDNF expression, potentially modulating fetal neuronal damage.
